studies.title: An Atom's Weight, Seen
studies.meaning: People come out in scattered groups, and the purpose is stated in the passive: to be shown their works. Not judged yet, shown. Then two lines with identical structure and one word changed, so the sentence about good and the sentence about evil are the same sentence. The unit of measurement is the smallest thing the language had, and the verb at the end is seeing rather than being told.
studies.historicalContext: Medinan by the tradition this collection follows, though the classical authorities differ and many place the surah in Mecca. No specific occasion is reported. It closes a chapter of eight short ayat in which the earth is shaken, gives up its weight, and then speaks, so the shown record arrives after the ground itself has testified.

keyTerms.note: Classically explained as the smallest ant or as the specks of dust visible in a sunbeam. It names the limit of what the eye can register, which is exactly the point of the sentence.
The plural of the word for what is dispersed, the same root used elsewhere of human efforts running in different directions. People arrive sorted rather than in one crowd.

A word from the scales, the standard weight a merchant set against goods. Pairing it with the smallest particle makes the image precise: the balance is calibrated far below anything a person would bother to record.

studies.lifeInProphetsTime: Merchants carried sets of weights and a balance, and the smallest weights were used for gold dust and for perfume, measured in quantities a customer had to trust the seller about. Disputes over a fraction were common. The image of a scale reading down to a mote spoke directly to people who knew exactly how much cheating happened at the bottom of a set of weights.
studies.didYouKnow: A report in the early collections describes the Prophet answering a long question about horses and their reward by reciting these two ayat and calling them the comprehensive, decisive statement. Two short lines were treated as sufficient for a question about something they do not mention, because the measure they set covers everything.
studies.theologicalSignificance: The symmetry of the two lines is the theology. Good and evil are weighed on the same scale, at the same resolution, with the same verb, so neither is treated as the default and neither is rounded away. That removes two comforts at once: the idea that small good deeds are not worth doing, and the idea that small wrongs do not count. The record is also shown rather than described, which makes the reckoning a matter of recognition.

crossReferences.why: Uses the same unit to describe God's justice, promising that nothing that small is mishandled.
Describes the same completeness from the other side, a book that omits nothing and the dismay of finding it so.
Applies the same smallness to hidden places, promising that a mustard seed is retrievable from anywhere.

studies.applyIt: Do one good thing today that is too small to mention: pick something off the floor, hold a door, send a two-word message. Then deliberately do not tell anyone. The scale in this ayah is calibrated below the level at which you would normally bother, which means most of your record is being written in a register you are not watching.
